children: Alphabet's Google is teaming up with Southern Co.'s subsidiary Georgia Power in an effort to advance nuclear energy in Georgia.
Under the agreement, Google plans to support uprates on Georgia Power's owned portion of nuclear units at two plants in the state, the companies said Monday.

The move will allow the facilities to add about 96 megawatts of new capacity to the electric grid to serve Georgia Power customers, and result in an estimated $900 million in projected benefits to customers over the life of the units, the companies said.
The agreement is subject to approval by the Georgia Public Service Commission.
Georgia Power, which is Southern Co.'s largest electric subsidiary, said the agreement is part of its efforts to help large customers meet their clean energy goals.
